title: Thoracic regional (T1-T4, T4-T8, T8-T12) extension ROM, seated, by sex
condition: healthy, seated with pelvis strapped, maximal active motion from upright sitting

quantity.name: regional primary ROM (extension)
quantity.definition: difference in angle between the two skin sensors bordering each region, neutral sitting to maximal motion

source.authors: Willems JM, Jull GA, Ng JK-F
source.sample: 60 healthy young adults, no thoracic pain/injury/surgery or respiratory disorder

protocol.summary: Regional thoracic primary rotations with Fastrak skin sensors at T1, T4, T8, T12; seated, pelvis fixed.
how_to_use: Use ≈ equal thirds of thoracic extension across T1-T4, T4-T8, T8-T12 (8.1/8.9/8.8 deg).
Use sex-specific rows when modelling a male or female subject (only rotation-left T8-T12 differs significantly by sex, p<0.005).
Seated, pelvis fixed: do not use for standing pelvis/lumbar sharing.

measurement.device: 3SPACE Fastrak, skin sensors on T1, T4, T8, T12 spinous processes; regional angle = difference between bordering sensors (Euler)
measurement.posture: seated on bench, lumbar support, pelvis and thighs belted, arms folded across chest
measurement.task: maximal active thoracic flexion, extension, lateral flexion L/R, axial rotation L/R from upright sitting

extraction.from: Table 1 (by sex, L/R separate) and Table 2 (pooled n=60, L/R averaged)
extraction.uncertainty: as printed (0.1 deg); repeatability error 1-3 deg (paper)
extraction.check_notes: Scanned PDF with noisy OCR: all values read from 350 dpi page images and compared twice; OCR misreads (e.g. '22.1 (6.31', '10.7 13.8)') resolved from images.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
